cards.definition: To guide a discussion back to where it should be.
cards.example:
- I had to steer the conversation back to the budget twice in twenty minutes.
Tive que direcionar a conversa de volta ao orçamento duas vezes em vinte minutos.
cards.note: Steer back to um assunto. Vem de dirigir: você segura o volante da conversa.

cards.translation: falar por cima, atropelar a fala do outro
cards.definition: To speak while another person is still speaking.
cards.example:
- Two directors talked over each other for ten minutes and decided nothing.
Dois diretores falaram por cima um do outro por dez minutos e não decidiram nada.
cards.note: Talk over someone é atropelar. Talk something over, com a coisa no meio, é conversar a respeito — outro verbo.

cards.definition: To give your opinion in a discussion, with some weight behind it.
cards.example:
- Can I weigh in on the timeline before we put it to a vote?
Posso me manifestar sobre o cronograma antes de levarmos a votação?
cards.note: Weigh in ON um assunto. É opinar com peso, não só comentar.

cards.translation: desviar do assunto, tirar do trilho
cards.definition: To pull a discussion away from its subject.
cards.example:
- One question about the logo sidetracked the entire meeting.
Uma pergunta sobre o logo desviou a reunião inteira.
cards.note: Quase sempre na passiva: we got sidetracked. O culpado é o assunto, não a pessoa.

cards.translation: tempo de fala (a fatia que cada um ocupa)
cards.definition: The share of the speaking time a person takes.
cards.example:
- Three people took all the airtime and the other five said nothing.
Três pessoas ficaram com todo o tempo de fala e as outras cinco não disseram nada.
cards.note: Incontável: more airtime, nunca airtimes. Vem do tempo de antena no rádio.

cards.translation: limitar o tempo de cada item
cards.definition: To set a fixed time limit for one item.
cards.example:
- We time-box every item at eight minutes, and the timer is on the screen.
A gente limita cada item em oito minutos, e o cronômetro fica na tela.
cards.note: Verbo e substantivo: a strict time-box. Com hífen; sem ele vira outra coisa.

cards.definition: A calm way of taking back the floor after being interrupted.
cards.example:
- Sorry — can I finish my thought? Two more sentences and it's yours.
Desculpa — posso terminar meu raciocínio? Mais duas frases e é sua.
cards.note: Dito com calma, devolve a palavra sem briga. O sorry na frente tira a aspereza e não pede desculpa de verdade.

cards.translation: Eu queria trazer a/o… para a conversa
cards.definition: A facilitator's move: inviting a specific person to speak, and saying why.
cards.example:
- I'd like to bring in Marta, who actually built the model we're arguing about.
Eu queria trazer a Marta, que foi quem construiu o modelo sobre o qual estamos discutindo.
cards.note: É o movimento de quem conduz: não pede opinião no vácuo, chama alguém pelo nome e diz por quê.

cards.definition: To believe something is true without checking it.
cards.example:
- Nobody weighed in because everyone assumed someone else would.
Ninguém se manifestou porque todo mundo presumiu que outra pessoa faria isso.
cards.note: Não é assumir no sentido de aceitar um cargo ou uma culpa — isso é take on ou take responsibility.

cards.definition: To back an idea or a person publicly.
cards.example:
- The people who agreed finally supported the point out loud.
Quem concordava finalmente apoiou o ponto em voz alta.
cards.note: Não é suportar no sentido de aguentar — isso é stand ou put up with.

questions.prompt: I had to _____ the conversation back to the budget twice.
questions.explanation: “Steer back to” a point the room has left.

options: He talked over of me twice.
He talked over to me twice.
questions.explanation: No preposition after “over”. And “talk something over” is a different verb — to discuss it.

questions.prompt: Can I _____ on the timeline before we vote?
One question about the logo pulled the meeting off topic. The meeting…
Three people took all the _____ and five said nothing.
We _____ every item at eight minutes.
questions.explanation: “Time-box AT” the limit; the hyphen stays.

questions.prompt: Sorry — _____ Two more sentences and it's yours.
questions.explanation: Said calmly, it returns the floor without a fight.

questions.prompt: _____ Marta, who actually built the model.
questions.explanation: Name the person and say why — that is what makes it work.

options: I assumed someone else would reply.
I assumed the new role in March.
She assumed responsibility for the loss.
He assumed the blame in public.
questions.answer: I assumed someone else would reply.
questions.explanation: “Assume” is to suppose. Taking on a role or blame is “take on” or “take responsibility”.
“Support” is to back. To tolerate is “stand” or “put up with”.
